title: jmap-types: too_many_changes_with_limit(limit) constructor
description:
Add a too_many_changes_with_limit constructor to JmapError so /changes handlers can emit a compliant tooManyChanges error with the required limit field per RFC 8620 section 9.6.1.

## Exact change — src/error.rs in crate-jmap-types

Add after the existing too_many_changes() constructor:

    /// Returns a tooManyChanges error with the server limit included.
    /// Per RFC 8620 §9.6.1, the limit field MUST be present so clients know
    /// the maximum maxChanges value to use on retry.
    pub fn too_many_changes_with_limit(limit: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            error_type: "tooManyChanges".into(),
            description: Some(limit.to_string()),
            existing_id: None,
        }
    }

NOTE: The limit value is packed into the description field because JmapError
has no generic extra-fields mechanism. The /changes handlers in jmap-mail-server
will serialize the limit separately in the response JSON — this constructor just
provides a typed way to carry the limit value through the error type.

ALTERNATIVE: If JmapError needs a proper limit field on the wire, add:
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub limit: Option<u64>,
to the JmapError struct and set it in the constructor. This is the RFC-compliant
approach and preferred if the struct change is acceptable.

Use the struct field approach (add limit: Option<u64>) since it produces correct wire output.

## Acceptance criteria
- cargo test -p jmap-types passes
- cargo clippy -p jmap-types -- -D warnings passes  
- JmapError::too_many_changes_with_limit(100) serializes to {"type":"tooManyChanges","limit":100}
- Existing too_many_changes() still works (limit field absent from its output)
- jmap-types is a locked crate — this is an explicitly authorized targeted change
